turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Hey Marcus, you got a sec? I need to confess something.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Uh oh. What did you break this time?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: So... I deployed the auth service this morning without running the test suite. I was in a rush, and I thought, 'what's the worst that could happen?'

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Joanna. Seriously? You know that's exactly how we got that regression last month. The one that slipped into production and broke login for half our users.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I know, I know. And I feel terrible. But I've already set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests. No more bypassing. It's mandatory now.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. That's actually a solid move. But did anything actually break this time?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: No, thankfully. Untested code never reached production — the deploy went through clean. But I'm not taking that risk again.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Alright, I'll hold you to that. And hey, while we're on the topic of risky moves — what's the deal with the new API endpoint you shipped? I heard it's been timing out under load.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah... that one's on me too. I shipped the API without pagination. It works fine for small requests, but once we hit real traffic, it just chokes. Timeouts everywhere.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Classic. Well, at least you're owning it. Let's get pagination in before the next release, okay?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Absolutely. I've already got a branch started. And this time, I'll run the tests. Promise.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, saw your PR for the pagination fix. Looks good. Did you run the full suite this time?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Ha, yes. Twice. And the CI gate is still active, so it wouldn't let me merge without passing anyway.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice. So we're good on the timeout issue?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Should be. I load-tested it with 500 concurrent users and it held up. No more API timing out under load.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Great. And just to be clear — you're not going to pull another 'deploy without tests' stunt, right?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Never again. That regression taught me a lesson. Plus, now the gate blocks me anyway. I literally can't merge without tests.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. That's the kind of self-sabotage prevention I like to see.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, well, better late than never. I just wish I'd done it before the whole production meltdown.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Live and learn. At least now we have a safety net.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Morning, Marcus. Quick update — the pagination fix is live, and I've also added a load test to the CI pipeline.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice. So we're covered on both fronts: no untested code, and no more timeouts.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. And I double-checked — the CI gate is still blocking any merge without tests. It's become second nature now.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Honestly, I'm impressed. You went from 'deploy and pray' to 'CI gate evangelist' in like a week.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Desperation is a great motivator. That regression slipping into production was embarrassing. I never want to be that person again.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Well, you're not. And the API is actually stable now. I checked the metrics this morning — zero timeouts.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Music to my ears. Thanks for not letting me off the hook, by the way. You could've just let me keep making mistakes.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nah, we're a team. Plus, I like sleeping at night without pager alerts.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Fair. Coffee's on me today.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Deal.
